item.title: aishore config check — validate config.yaml and print effective values
item.intent: Users must be able to run 'aishore config check' and see every effective configuration value with its source (default/config/env), and any validation errors in config.yaml must be reported explicitly.
item.description: Users who edit config.yaml have no way to validate it before running a sprint. Unknown keys are silently ignored (load_config falls back to defaults), type errors produce cryptic runtime failures, and there's no way to see what the effective configuration actually is. A 'config check' command would: parse config.yaml (warn if missing), validate known keys and value types, flag unknown keys, and print a table of all effective values (merged from config.yaml + env vars). This removes a class of 'why isn't my config working' support issues and makes the configuration surface visible.
steps: Add cmd_config_check() function: read config.yaml via yq (if available) or fallback parser
Validate each key against the known config schema (agent_model, timeout, maturity.enabled, scope.mode, permissions.*, etc.) — log_warn on unknown keys
For each known config key, determine effective value: env var > config.yaml > default, and note source
Print a table: KEY | EFFECTIVE VALUE | SOURCE (env/config/default)
Exit 1 if config.yaml exists but cannot be parsed; exit 0 if config is valid or missing
Wire 'config check' as a top-level command in main dispatch and add to help text
acceptanceCriteria: Running 'aishore config check' with no config.yaml prints all defaults with source=default
Running 'aishore config check' with a valid config.yaml shows overridden keys with source=config
Running 'aishore config check' with an env var set shows that key with source=env
Unknown keys in config.yaml produce a warning line in output
A malformed config.yaml (invalid YAML) exits 1 with a clear error
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
